title: Insider Fraud and First-Party Fraud
summary: Fraud committed by employees, contractors and the firm's own customers, how it is concealed, and the controls, culture and investigation practices that reduce it.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Fraud committed by employees, contractors and the firm's own customers, how it is concealed, and the controls, culture and investigation practices that reduce it.
Learning Objectives: Identify insider fraud risk across roles, systems and third parties
Recognise first-party fraud, including false claims and mule activity
Apply proportionate investigation and response to suspected cases
Syllabus: Insider threat: access, opportunity, pressure and rationalisation
Preventive controls: segregation of duties, access reviews and vetting
First-party fraud: false claims, refund abuse and complicit mules
Intended Audience: Fraud prevention, fraud operations and investigations teams
Payments operations, customer service and complaints staff who handle suspected fraud cases
Compliance, financial crime and risk staff, and managers accountable for fraud outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, payments operations or financial crime compliance is helpful. No technical background in data analytics is required.
Core Reading: FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)
